belief: My worth depends on my success.
origins: Praise for good grades, wins, promotions, and paychecks teaches that we are loved for what we achieve. In competitive cultures, success becomes the scorecard of worth, and failure feels like personal defect. Even in church, the successful may be applauded most.
teaches: Paul writes, “For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God, not by works, so that no one can boast.” Jesus asks, “What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?” “I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” Our worth was established before we achieved anything. Work is good, and diligence matters, but they are expressions of life, not its foundation.
self_statements: If I stop succeeding, I am nothing.
My value goes up and down with results.
I have to keep proving myself.
Failure means I am a failure.
I have to win to matter.
errors: Believing I am either a success or a failure.
Calling myself a failure after a setback.
Feeling worthless after a loss and concluding that I am.
Insisting that I must always succeed.
questions: When did I first learn that success earns love?
Who loves me whether I succeed or not?
What would I be if I lost my title, income, or achievements?
What does Scripture say about the basis of my worth?
What do I do when I fail?
What is one thing I can enjoy this week without measuring it?
truth: My worth does not rise and fall with my success. I am loved by God and saved by grace. I can work hard and enjoy the fruit, while resting in a worth that was given and cannot be taken.
hw_truths: I am saved by grace, not works.
My worth was given before I achieved.
I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
My labor in the Lord is not in vain.
I am loved when I fail.
log: Each week, note one thing you did without needing it to prove anything.
actions: Write who taught you that success earns worth.
Write who you are without it.
List five things true of you apart from achievements.
Try something you might not be good at.
prayer: Father, I have measured myself by success. Thank You that You saved me by grace. Free me to work with joy and rest in the worth You have given. Amen.
hw_questions: Who taught me success earns worth?
What would I be without my achievements?
What do I do when I fail?
What can I enjoy without measuring?
